curation_basis: Actual rendered pages from the two registered, hash-verified benchmark PDFs were visually inspected at full resolution on 2026-10-19.

allowed: color, ornament, typography hierarchy and emotional staging reference
forbidden: treating benchmark story content as DM04 source evidence
transferring benchmark deities, characters, weapons, mounts, flags or theology into DM04
assuming a known shortcoming is approved merely because it appears in a benchmark

extraction.normalization: NONE; pages preserve the raster dimensions emitted from the exact PDF page at 72 dpi
extraction.oversized_blob_policy: Source PDFs remain ignored local references; only the eight selected page PNGs are tracked and every one is below 100 MiB.

pages.source_book: Sri Satyanarayana Vrata Katha — Complete Illustrated Storybook
pages.selection_reason: A complete series cover with immediate devotional focus, strong foreground-to-background depth and a disciplined navy/gold identity.
composition_principles: title kept distinct from the sacred focal face
expression_qualities: devotees shown through directed gaze and gesture
storytelling_characteristics: cover establishes devotion and place without pretending to be a story panel
cultural_iconographic_constraints: Vishnu's identity and attributes are reference content only
do not transfer temple, river or devotee details without current-story support
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: cover hierarchy is not a substitute for sequential interior storytelling
dense ornament must not crowd later lettering

pages.source_book: Sri Satyanarayana Vrata Katha — Complete Illustrated Storybook
pages.selection_reason: It moves from assembly to question, divine answer and a focused teaching exchange through purposeful changes of scale.
composition_principles: wide establishing panel above paired speaker panels
close response scene before informational inset
expression_qualities: curiosity, attention and calm explanation are visible in faces and hands
storytelling_characteristics: each panel changes speaker, scale or information
caption and speech have different jobs
cultural_iconographic_constraints: Narada, Vishnu and their attributes must not transfer to DM04
any halo or celestial prop still requires current-story review
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: several passages are dense at normal reading size
AI-rendered lettering would require exact relettering
repeated divine portraits vary slightly

pages.source_book: Sri Satyanarayana Vrata Katha — Complete Illustrated Storybook
pages.selection_reason: A grounded Indian domestic story in which gesture, market detail, family response and the home ritual make the emotional change legible.
qualities_to_preserve: ritual objects placed as story evidence
composition_principles: large lower ritual scene as resolution
expression_qualities: surprise, gratitude and household joy read without exaggerated caricature
storytelling_characteristics: cause, action and result are separated into distinct scenes
cultural_iconographic_constraints: ritual practice and Vishnu image belong to this story
do not generalize one village or domestic style as canonical for all eras
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: the final moral is more declarative than necessary
dense small details can compete with text
material prosperity is visually simplified

pages.source_book: Sri Satyanarayana Vrata Katha — Complete Illustrated Storybook
pages.selection_reason: The page carries grief, prayer, release, renewed peril and reverent resolution across changing places while keeping the sequence readable.
qualities_to_preserve: contrasting palace, ritual, harbor and storm environments
composition_principles: final reverence scene closes the sequence
color_characteristics: warm gold devotional scenes contrasted with cold slate storm blues
expression_qualities: grief, petition, relief, alarm and reverence remain distinct
storytelling_characteristics: locations and emotional states change panel by panel without losing causality
lettering_approach: moral kept in a separate closing box
cultural_iconographic_constraints: ritual objects and divine identity are story-bound
ships and court dress are illustrative conventions, not asserted historical reconstruction
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: five beats create a crowded page
some text is small
maritime details are generalized rather than evidence of a precise period

pages.source_book: The Enemy Who Multiplied — Original-Size Comic Pages
pages.selection_reason: Two large conversational panels and two reaction close-ups turn a proposal into a threat through pose, expression and scale rather than a single poster-like tableau.
color_characteristics: vermilion and emerald against cool Himalayan depth
storytelling_characteristics: reaction is given its own visual beat
lettering_approach: editable-looking oval balloons with speaker tails
cultural_iconographic_constraints: the Goddess, lion, Sugriva and Himalayan terrace are DM08 content
a relaxed two-arm depiction cannot override another scene's many-arm requirement
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: balloons are text-heavy
architecture and jewelry are generalized
facial continuity requires close inspection across pages

pages.source_book: The Enemy Who Multiplied — Original-Size Comic Pages
pages.selection_reason: The page separates approach, inward change, full manifestation and battlefield consequence into four legible beats with a forceful central reveal.
color_characteristics: deep black hair and blue-violet skin
expression_qualities: righteous anger changes visibly into decisive action
opponents react rather than pose generically
storytelling_characteristics: manifestation is a sequence, not several contradictory moments compressed into one still
lettering_approach: balloons placed inside their action panel
cultural_iconographic_constraints: Kali/Chamunda's appearance, skull garland, tongue and weapons are source-specific and must not transfer to DM04 Devī
demonic-face flags require separate source support
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: blood and severed-body emphasis may exceed family-appropriate limits
unsupported demonic-face flag emblems appear
crowded limbs and weapons require anatomy review

pages.source_book: The Enemy Who Multiplied — Original-Size Comic Pages
pages.selection_reason: It explains a battlefield rule through a hero entrance, visible consequence, narrator-frame interpretation and a specific new clash.
qualities_to_preserve: narrator frame integrated into battle pacing
color_characteristics: red-gold antagonist against blue mountain depth
navy/gold structure keeps dense action coherent
expression_qualities: defiance, danger recognition and analytical concern are distinct
storytelling_characteristics: battle mechanism is shown and then interpreted
consequence does not replace source explanation
cultural_iconographic_constraints: Raktabija, Aindri, the elephant mount and blood-multiplication mechanism are DM08 content only
flag symbols and military equipment need current-source review
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: blood multiplication is graphically prominent
unsupported demonic-face flags recur
some helmets and armor drift toward generic fantasy

pages.source_book: The Enemy Who Multiplied — Original-Size Comic Pages
pages.selection_reason: A climactic page gives the source mechanism, its completion, divine relief and the narrator-frame release separate visual beats while maintaining a unified page identity.
qualities_to_preserve: figures remain expressive at multiple scales
expression_qualities: effort, ferocity, relief and reflection are separated rather than blended
storytelling_characteristics: action, consequence and aftermath receive distinct panels
the final human breath prevents poster-like closure
cultural_iconographic_constraints: Chandika, Chamunda, the Mothers, Raktabija and their equipment are DM08-only content
no deity or weapon may transfer into DM04 through style conditioning
known_shortcomings_not_to_copy: graphic blood treatment exceeds DM04's family-appropriate target
many simultaneous weapons create crowding
unsupported flag emblems remain visible
dense text reduces breathing room
